description: Cloud Sync end-to-end encryption known answers (WIRE-CONTRACT-V5 section 13.10, section 13.8.1; plans/CC-01-cloud-sync.md section 2.4). A client table, inert to an SDK that has not implemented sync.e2e: a runner reads the named sections it implements. Every row is recomputed by the generator through an independent reference over node:crypto. hkdfCases: HKDF-SHA256 with the exact ikm, salt, info and length, anchored by RFC 5869 appendix A; the label field names the derivation and the info bytes are shown in hex because several labels end in a NUL. envelopeCases: pkey-sync-value/1; a runner opens envelopeHex under rootHex, collection, name and aliases and expects `expect`, and for rows with a `seal` member also seals value with that salt and expects the same bytes (canonical JSON with sorted keys, UTF-8, padded 0x80 then zeros to a multiple of 64, always at least one byte); the invalid reasons are shape, version, kid, auth, padding, json and name, in the order a reader checks them. blindCases: blind(kind, ctx, n). transferPlanCases: the upload mode, partBytes and part count from the stored size and the collection's files.delta. hpkeAnchor: the RFC 9180 vector for pkey-sync-wrap/1 (enc, shared_secret, key, base_nonce and ciphertext). wrapCases: pkey-sync-wrap/1; a runner unwraps wrap (kem as an integer, enc and ct in hex) for recipientPrivateHex under product, deviceId, ringId and epoch with kidHex as aad and expects expectRootHex (null is a refusal); a `seal` member also wraps rootHex to recipientPublicHex with the ephemeral private key and expects the same enc and ct, and infoHex is the exact HPKE info. recoveryCodeCases: kind code (codeHex encodes to text, text parses to codeHex), kind parse (input parses to expectCodeHex or null) and kind blob (recovery.ct under K_rec; the same open/seal rule, with seal giving rootHex and nonceHex). The text is 8 hyphenated groups of 4 Crockford base32 characters over the code and the first 4 bytes of its SHA-256. adoptCases: the adopt blob (0x01, nonce, AES-256-GCM under K_adopt of currentRootHex, aad = pkey-sync/1 adopt, fromRingId, u32be(epoch), kid); expectRootHex is the adopted root or null. cdcCases: fastcdc-2016-nc1 (xorshift32 gear table from seed 0x9e3779b9; the hash starts at 0 at offset min of each chunk): a runner builds the input (stream: SHA-256(UTF-8 of `pkey-sync vector cdc ` + label, u32be counter) blocks cut to length; byte: length copies of value), cuts it with avg (min = avg/4, max = avg*4) and expects the chunk lengths in lens. chunkCases: kind id (the E2E id is HMAC-SHA256(K_cid(collection), chunk) and the server id SHA-256(chunk), both lowercase hex) and kind object (pkey-sync-chunk/1 under the 32 raw id bytes: open and expect; a `seal` member also seals bodyHex with that codec and expects objectHex; the invalid reasons are shape, version, codec, auth, decode, size and id in the order a reader checks; the codec 1 frames here are raw-block zstd frames). fileStreamCases: pkey-sync-file/1 (header little-endian, nonce counter big-endian; the plaintext of a seal row is SHA-256(UTF-8 of `pkey-sync vector file ` + label, u32be counter) blocks cut to length; the salt is in the row). kind seal: seal that plaintext under rootHex and collection with saltHex and expect sealedSize, headerHex, sealedSha256Hex and plainSha256Hex (and sealedHex when present). kind sizes: plainToSealed pairs and sealedToPlain pairs (null: no stream has that size). kind open: take the sealed stream of the row named by base (a seal row), apply the mutate ops in order (truncate length; dropSegment index; swapSegments a b; appendSegment from; xor offset value; setHex offset hex; appendHex hex; segment i starts at 64 + i * (1 MiB + 16)), open it under openCollection (default collection) expecting the kid derived from the root unless expectKidHex is given, and expect ok with plainSha256Hex or a refusal; the reasons are shape, magic, version, flags, segmentSize, kid, size and auth in that order (auth covers truncation, reordering, a missing last flag and a tampered header). kind range: the same stored stream, open plaintext [start, end) through a reader that sees only offset and length; expect ok with length, sha256Hex and the exact reads (the header first, then one per segment overlapped, in order) or a refusal (range adds to the reasons). Only the segments read are authenticated; the stored size alone says which is last. manifestCases: pkey-sync-chunks/1 parse (ok rows are also re-encoded to the same bytes); the invalid reasons are shape, magic, version, recordSize, flags, reserved, count, length, size, record, chunkLen and a final size for the sum, first violation wins. Append-only: a new row or section keeps syncVectorsVersion; a changed row or rule bumps it.

hkdfCases.description: RFC 5869 appendix A.1: the published known answer, so the reference is anchored outside this file.
hkdfCases.label: rfc5869

hkdfCases.description: RFC 5869 appendix A.3: empty salt and empty info (an empty salt is 32 zero bytes).
hkdfCases.label: rfc5869

hkdfCases.description: kid = HKDF(R, empty, 'pkey-sync/1 kid', 16): in every envelope header, in the clear.
hkdfCases.label: kid

hkdfCases.description: K_coll('$settings'): the info is the label, a NUL, then the collection name.
hkdfCases.label: coll

hkdfCases.description: K_coll for a concrete collection name.
hkdfCases.label: coll

hkdfCases.description: K_cid(c): keys the chunk ids of one collection.
hkdfCases.label: chunk-id

hkdfCases.description: K_msg: one key per value, from K_coll and a fresh 16-byte salt.
hkdfCases.label: value

hkdfCases.description: K_file: one key per file version, from K_coll and a 32-byte salt.
hkdfCases.label: file

hkdfCases.description: K_chunk: one key per chunk id (the 32 raw bytes of the id are the salt).
hkdfCases.label: chunk

hkdfCases.description: K_rec: the recovery code (16 bytes) is the key material and the ringId text is the salt.
hkdfCases.label: recovery

hkdfCases.description: K_adopt: wraps a foreign root after an account merge.
hkdfCases.label: adopt

blindCases.description: An open-setting key under the declared key that scopes it.
A merge member name: ctx is the declared merge setting.
A record id: ctx is the collection.
A field name inside a record collection.
A union element is its canonical JSON.
A person-chosen id with non-ASCII text.
An empty name is still blinded.
Same ctx and name as 'record-slot-1', another kind: a different value.
Same kind and name as 'record-slot-1', another ctx: a different value.
The 0x00 separators frame the fields; a one-character ctx and name.

transferPlanCases.description: An empty file is a single PUT.
Exactly 16 MiB is still one PUT.
One byte over 16 MiB: multipart with 8 MiB parts (3 parts).
1 GiB: ceil(size / 9,999) is 107,386 bytes, rounded up to 1 MiB, below the 8 MiB floor.
A size that is an exact multiple of the part size has no short part.
files.delta, but under 1 MiB: not chunked, single.
files.delta and 500 MiB: chunks, never multipart.
files.delta off and 1 MiB: still single.
One byte over 1 GiB is refused (SYNC_FILE_MAX_BYTES).
The cap applies to chunked collections too.

hpkeAnchor.note: RFC 9180 test vector for mode_base, KEM 0x0020, KDF 0x0001 and AEAD 0x0002, copied from the pinned upstream file (sequence 0 only; hex). `source.sha256` pins the whole upstream file, `sha256` the vector as sorted-key compact JSON. A runner checks enc, shared_secret, key, base_nonce and the ciphertext; the raw layout (enc, then ciphertext followed by the tag) is what CryptoKit and Tink expose.

wrapCases.description: A root wrapped to a device key; sealing it again with the ephemeral key gives the same bytes.
Another epoch is another info and another wrap.
The product is part of info.
The device id is part of info.
The ring id is part of info.
The epoch is part of info.
The kid is the associated data.
A different recipient key cannot open it.
A flipped ciphertext bit fails authentication.
A flipped tag bit fails authentication.
A flipped encapsulated-key bit derives another key.
An encapsulated key must be 32 bytes.
An all-zero encapsulated key is refused.

recoveryCodeCases.description: Another first character fails the checksum.
U is not in the alphabet.
The root sealed under the code; sealing again with the nonce gives the same bytes.
The ring id is the salt and part of aad.
The epoch is part of aad.
The kid is part of aad.

adoptCases.description: A previous root sealed under K_adopt of the current one; sealing again with the nonce gives the same bytes.
Another current root derives another K_adopt.
The source ring id is part of aad.
The source epoch is part of aad.
The source kid is part of aad.
A blob sealed under K_rec with a recovery aad does not open as an adopt blob.

cdcCases.description: An empty input has no chunks.
An input of exactly min (avg / 4) bytes is one chunk: a remainder of at most min is never cut.
One byte past min: the scan starts at offset min and sees one byte.
An input of exactly max (avg * 4) bytes of zeros: the gear hash of zeros never meets either mask, so the cut is at max.
One byte past max: a max chunk and a one-byte remainder.
3 MiB of zeros at the real parameters: three max chunks.
Pseudo-random input, avg 1 KiB (min 256, max 4 KiB).
Pseudo-random input, avg 4 KiB (min 1 KiB, max 16 KiB).
Pseudo-random input at the real parameters: avg 256 KiB, min 64 KiB, max 1 MiB.
The same stream cut 100 bytes shorter: the cuts before the tail are unchanged.

chunkCases.description: E2E id is HMAC-SHA256(K_cid(c), chunk); server id is SHA-256(chunk).
Ids are defined for an empty chunk too (the manifest refuses such a record).
The same plaintext in another collection has another E2E id (K_cid is per collection) and the same server id.
codec 0: 0x01 0x00, then AES-256-GCM of the chunk under K_chunk(id), nonce zero, aad = 0x01 0x00 id.
codec 1: the body is one zstd frame with its content size (here raw blocks); a reader decodes both codecs.
Codec 2 is unknown (checked before any decryption).
A flipped bit in the tag.
Codec 0 relabelled 1: the codec is in the associated data.
A chunk object opened under another id.
A chunk object opened in another collection.
Codec 1 whose body is not a zstd frame.
Codec 1 whose frame header declares no content size.
Codec 1 whose frame declares 2 MiB: refused before decoding (max is 1 MiB).
Sealed under idA with a body that is not the chunk idA names: it opens, and the keyed hash of the plaintext differs from the id.

fileStreamCases.description: An empty file is one empty last segment: the header and a 16-byte tag.
One byte: one last segment.
1 MiB - 1: one short last segment.
Exactly 1 MiB: one full segment that is the last; no empty segment follows.
1 MiB + 1: a full segment (flag 0, counter 0) and a one-byte last segment (flag 1, counter 1).
Exactly 2 MiB: two full segments, only the second last.
2.5 MiB: two full segments and a half-size last.
plainSize -> sealedSize = 64 + plainSize + 16 * max(1, ceil(plainSize / 1 MiB)); a sealed size no stream has maps to null.
Opens seal-empty.
Opens seal-one-byte.
Opens seal-segment-minus-one.
Opens seal-segment-exact.
Opens seal-segment-plus-one.
Opens seal-two-segments-exact.
Opens seal-three-segments.
The last segment dropped: the new final segment was sealed with last = 0, so its tag fails as the last.
The stream cut inside the last segment.
Only the header remains: no segment at all.
Fewer than 64 bytes.
A tail shorter than a tag.
The two full segments swapped: each was sealed under its own counter.
The first and the last segment swapped (the stream length changes too).
A full segment appended after the last: the old last now fails as a non-last.
The first segment removed: the rest are one counter short.
An empty last segment after a full one is refused before any tag is tried: only the empty file has one.
The first segment of a two-segment file standing alone: it was sealed with last = 0, so it fails as a last segment.
One bit flipped in the first segment.
One bit flipped in the last tag.
A flipped salt byte changes K_file, so every segment fails.
Opened under another collection's K_coll.
The magic is not PKSYNCF1.
version u16 (little-endian) is 2.
flags u16 is not 0: no flag is defined.
segmentBytes u32 (little-endian) is 64 KiB, not 1 MiB.
segmentBytes written big-endian (00 10 00 00) reads as 4096 little-endian and is refused.
The header's kid is not the kid of the ring the reader holds.
A flipped kid byte in the header.
Bytes 0..100 read the header and segment 0 only.
start = end reads only the header.
A range inside segment 1.
A range across the segment 0 / 1 boundary reads two segments.
end exactly at a boundary reads only segment 0.
start exactly at a boundary reads only segment 1.
The tail of a short last segment: its read length is its actual length.
The whole plaintext reads every segment.
A file of exactly 1 MiB: segment 0 is the last.
The empty file has an empty range only.
end is past the plaintext size.
start is after end.
A flipped bit in segment 2 does not touch a range inside segment 0: only the segments read are authenticated.
The same flip, with a range that reads segment 2.
A stream cut at a segment boundary has another size, so the size alone moves the last flag: a range in segment 1 now fails.
A stored size no stream has is refused before any read.

manifestCases.description: An empty file: no records, plainSize 0, the SHA-256 of nothing.
Three records, one id twice: file order, duplicates allowed (content repeats).
chunkCount 16,385 (over SYNC_MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FILE), checked before the length.
A record's flags are not zero.
A record's reserved is not zero.
The records do not add up to plainSize.
Bad magic and bad version: magic.
Bad flags and a short body: flags comes first.
Count over the cap and a short body: count.
A bad flag in record 2 and a zero length in record 1: record 1 is checked first, so chunkLen.
A zero length also breaks the sum: chunkLen.
